From 4f1a02e75a2eedfddd10222c0fe61d2a04d80099 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Marco Chiappero <marco.chiappero@intel.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jan 2021 15:35:15 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] crypto: qat - replace CRYPTO_AES with CRYPTO_LIB_AES in
 Kconfig

Use CRYPTO_LIB_AES in place of CRYPTO_AES in the dependences for the QAT
common code.

Fixes: c0e583ab2016 ("crypto: qat - add CRYPTO_AES to Kconfig dependencies")
Reported-by: Ard Biesheuvel <ardb@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Marco Chiappero <marco.chiappero@intel.com>
Acked-by: Ard Biesheuvel <ardb@kernel.org>
Reviewed-by: Giovanni Cabiddu <giovanni.cabiddu@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>

diff --git a/drivers/crypto/qat/Kconfig b/drivers/crypto/qat/Kconfig
index 846a3d90b41a..77783feb62b2 100644
--- a/drivers/crypto/qat/Kconfig
+++ b/drivers/crypto/qat/Kconfig
@@ -11,7 +11,7 @@ config CRYPTO_DEV_QAT
 	select CRYPTO_SHA1
 	select CRYPTO_SHA256
 	select CRYPTO_SHA512
-	select CRYPTO_AES
+	select CRYPTO_LIB_AES
 	select FW_LOADER
 
 config CRYPTO_DEV_QAT_DH895xCC
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/crypto/qat/Kconfig`**
   - The line `select CRYPTO_AES` has been replaced with `select CRYPTO_LIB_AES`. This change updates the dependency for the QAT common code to use `CRYPTO_LIB_AES` instead of `CRYPTO_AES`.

### Relationships
- The modification in the `Kconfig` file addresses a dependency issue by ensuring that the QAT common code correctly references `CRYPTO_LIB_AES`, which is a more appropriate dependency than `CRYPTO_AES`. This change is part of a bug fix that was reported and acknowledged by other developers, indicating a collaborative effort to improve the codebase. The fix is linked to a previous commit that added `CRYPTO_AES` as a dependency, which was deemed incorrect.

Reviewed-by: Giovanni Cabiddu <giovanni.cabiddu@intel.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by incorrectly using `CRYPTO_AES` as a dependency in the QAT common code, which should have referenced `CRYPTO_LIB_AES` instead. This misconfiguration could lead to issues in the functionality of the QAT driver, as it relies on the correct cryptographic library being selected for proper operation.
